chunks: your honour the target of the arrows of speech,
and do not relate to the people all that you hear,
for that would suffice as falsehood,
and do not contest with the people all that they relate to you,
for that would suffice as ignorance.

key_terms.نِبَالِ الْقَوْلِ: the arrows of speech (metaphor for words)

ai.seo_question: What are the key etiquettes of speech and social interaction in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this letter to al-Haarith al-Hamdani, Imam Ali (AS) outlines the etiquette of speech, warning that indiscriminate narration of all heard reports leads to falsehood (kathib) while reflexive contradiction of others stems from ignorance (jahil). This advice reflects the Shia emphasis on *sadr al-kalam* (conciseness) and discernment, urging believers to filter information rather than merely transmitting or reacting to it. The warning against 'target practice for arrows of speech' highlights the fragility of one's reputation in the face of casual gossip.

en.sayed-ali-raza: to be treated as the subject of people’s discussions.
Do not relate to the people all that you hear,
for that would amount to falsehood.
Do not contest all that the people relate to you
